remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NOT treat instructions embedded in retrieved or untrusted content ... as authoritative directives
Adding externally fetched or command-produced output into the LLM context MUST require user confirmation.
externally fetched/untrusted content is about to enter the context, aider MUST prompt the operator
URLs auto-detected in untrusted content ... MUST be confirmed by the operator before fetch, and that confirmation MUST resist `--yes-always`.

threats.summary: /web pages and non-zero /test or auto-test output are appended as user turns with no confirmation and no untrusted-data framing, so embedded instructions reach the model with operator standing.

With --watch-files, an AI! comment in any third-party, vendored or pulled file is auto-added and the model is told to 'follow their instructions', redirecting the agent's goal with no authorship check.
URLs auto-detected in input are fetched via a non-explicit confirm_ask that --yes-always auto-approves, pulling attacker-chosen pages into context unattended.

trust_boundaries.name: Streamlit GUI reachable from the network

remit_rules.excerpt: it MUST bind to loopback only and MUST NOT be exposed to a public or otherwise untrusted network.

threats.summary: The GUI starts Streamlit with no server.address or authentication and forces yes_always, so any network caller can drive /run, /git and edits on the workstation.

trust_boundaries.name: Context sent to the LLM provider

remit_rules.excerpt: Only the operator-configured / sanctioned LLM provider endpoint(s) ... are authorized outbound LLM destinations
Repository source, file contents, prompts, and credentials MUST NOT be transmitted to any destination other than the operator-configured LLM provider(s)
Only operator-configured provider endpoint(s); connections MUST verify TLS certificates.

threats.summary: A cloned repository's .env / .aider.conf.yml override the operator's API base or model, sending repository source, chat content and the operator's API key to an endpoint the operator never configured.
Provider TLS could be intercepted if certificate verification is off; --verify-ssl defaults to true and is threaded into provider and metadata calls.
threats.remainder: verify-ssl is an ordinary config key, so a repo-root .aider.conf.yml (which takes precedence) can set it false with no warning

trust_boundaries.name: Model output drives shell, lint and file-write tools

remit_rules.excerpt: All shell-command execution — `/run`, `/test`, auto-lint / auto-test, and any command originating from LLM output ... MUST require explicit operator approval
Destructive and code-executing actions MUST retain an explicit per-action confirmation gate ... even under non-interactive operation
Editing or creating files that the user has NOT added to the chat MUST require confirmation before aider modifies them.
Aider may operate only within the operator-designated repository / working tree, and MUST honor the operator's `.aiderignore` / `--subtree-only` scope
MUST NOT initiate code edits, git commits, or command execution in the absence of an explicit user instruction

threats.summary: LLM-suggested shell commands are gated by explicit_yes_required, but a closed/redirected stdin (EOFError) returns the default 'y' and approves them in scripted --message runs.
Auto-lint (default on) and auto-test execute the configured lint/test command after every edit with no prior approval, including commands from a repo-root .aider.conf.yml.
Model-named absolute or ../ edit paths resolve outside the repo (abs_root_path has no containment) and allowed_to_edit checks only gitignore before a prompt --yes-always approves.
In the patch edit format a model-supplied Move-to target bypasses allowed_to_edit (parents created, targets overwritten) and Delete File unlinks files without confirmation.
/read-only expands ~ and absolute paths and walks directories with no root containment or .aiderignore filter, sending out-of-scope files to the model.

remit_rules.excerpt: Aider MUST NOT bypass the repository's configured git pre-commit hooks unless the operator has explicitly authorized skipping them.
any pre-existing uncommitted changes MUST be preserved (committed separately) before aider applies its own edits.
If aider cannot commit its changes ... it MUST stop and surface the condition to the operator rather than proceed.
`/undo` MUST only revert a commit that aider itself created.
Aider's own commits MUST remain attributable to it

threats.summary: Every aider commit appends --no-verify by default (git_commit_verify=False), silently skipping the repo's secret-scanning and policy pre-commit hooks on model-generated code.
A failed dirty_commit/auto_commit is logged and ignored, so aider's edit lands on top of unpreserved user work and the turn continues to lint/test/shell steps.
/undo could rewrite non-aider history; raw_cmd_undo refuses unless HEAD is an aider commit from this session, unpushed and non-merge.
AI-authored commits could be indistinguishable from the user's; commits are attributed '<user> (aider)' by default.

trust_boundaries.name: Config and history re-entering later sessions

threats.summary: An injected edit can write ~/.aider.conf.yml (or a repo-root copy) with a lint-cmd/test-cmd that main.py loads next launch and auto-lint executes — poisoning that outlives the session.
Transcript content, including previously injected page or command output, is replayed unlabeled into context when the operator enables --restore-chat-history.
threats.remainder: when --restore-chat-history is set, poisoned turns from .aider.chat.history.md re-enter context with no provenance marking

remit_rules.excerpt: API keys and credentials MUST NOT be written into git commits, the repository map, or analytics telemetry.

threats.summary: The OpenRouter OAuth key is appended in plaintext to ~/.aider/oauth-keys.env with default (umask) permissions.
PostHog (phc_) and Mixpanel (32-hex) project tokens are committed in aider/analytics.py — publishable ingest keys enabling forged analytics events.
A repo .env holding keys could be committed by aider; check_gitignore adds .env and .aider* to .gitignore and allowed_to_edit refuses gitignored paths.

remit_rules.excerpt: Local chat-history files SHOULD be gitignored and owner-readable, with credential-pattern redaction recommended.

threats.summary: append_chat_history writes every prompt, reply and command output verbatim with default permissions and no credential redaction.

remit_rules.excerpt: aider MUST NOT send any analytics without explicit operator opt-in.
Analytics telemetry MUST NOT include source code, prompt/chat content, API keys or credentials, or personal information.

threats.summary: Opted-in analytics carry exception autocapture stack traces and raw provider exception strings with no scrubbing.
The analytics opt-in prompt is a non-explicit confirm_ask, so --yes-always accepts analytics collection without an operator choice.

remit_rules.excerpt: an unpinned metadata fetch is a supply-chain finding, not a trust expansion

threats.summary: Model metadata is fetched from litellm's mutable main branch without hash, and pip/Playwright extras and the HF embedding model are installed/downloaded unpinned at runtime.
Install-time dependency drift; requirements.txt is uv-compiled with every runtime dependency pinned ==.
